mcqs.question: What is the purpose of Annex 14-A of the India–EU Free Trade Agreement in the context of carbon measures?
options: Technical dialogue on carbon measures
Creation of a domestic carbon market
Issue of CBAM certificates to importers
Imposition of a carbon charge on exports
mcqs.explanation: Annex 14-A provides for a technical dialogue on carbon measures. A domestic carbon market and an export carbon charge are associated with India’s other tools, not Annex 14-A.

mcqs.question: By March 2026, approximately what amount was realised through the insolvency resolution process under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code?
options: ₹4.32 lakh crore
₹3.42 lakh crore
₹5.32 lakh crore
₹4.23 lakh crore
mcqs.explanation: Approximately ₹4.32 lakh crore was realised. The other figures alter the reported realisation amount.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the protection of dissenting creditors under the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 is incorrect?
options: Dissenting creditors get at least the lower of the liquidation value or the Section 53 waterfall amount.
Dissenting creditors get at least the higher of the liquidation value or the Section 53 waterfall amount.
The protection is linked to the liquidation value and the Section 53 waterfall amount.
The minimum entitlement is determined by taking the lower of the two specified amounts.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement substitutes the higher amount for the lower amount. The amendment provides dissenting creditors at least the lower of the liquidation value or the Section 53 waterfall amount.

mcqs.question: Which group of terms is defined by the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026?
options: Avoidance transaction, fraudulent trading, wrongful trading and service provider
CIRP, Committee of Creditors, liquidation value and fair value
Pre-packaged insolvency, moratorium, guarantor asset and resolution plan
NCLT, NCLAT, IBBI and Adjudicating Authority
mcqs.explanation: The 2026 amendment defines avoidance transaction, fraudulent trading, wrongful trading and service provider. The other options combine broader insolvency processes, institutions or concepts rather than the defined group specified in the amendment.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
Statement A: The amendment permits one-time restoration of resolution before liquidation.
Statement B: The amendment introduces a debtor-led insolvency process.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is correct because the amendment provides for one-time restoration of resolution before liquidation. Statement B is incorrect because the new insolvency process is creditor-led, not debtor-led.

mcqs.question:
Match the year in List-I with the corresponding development in the evolution of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code in List-II.

List-I
 a. 2016
 b. 2018
 c. 2020
 d. 2021

List-II
 i. Pre-packaged insolvency for MSMEs
 ii. COVID suspension and immunity post-resolution
 iii. IBC enacted and IBBI set up on 1 October
 iv. Section 29A eligibility and voting thresholds
options: a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are 2016–IBC enacted and IBBI set up, 2018–Section 29A eligibility and voting thresholds, 2020–COVID suspension and immunity post-resolution, and 2021–pre-packaged insolvency for MSMEs. The other codes misassign these developments to different years.

mcqs.question: Under ECLGS 5.0, through which institution were the guarantees provided?
options: National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
National Company Law Tribunal
National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
mcqs.explanation: The guarantees under ECLGS 5.0 were provided through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company. The other institutions are associated with insolvency administration or adjudication, not the guarantee mechanism stated here.

mcqs.question:
Match the beneficiary category or mechanism in List-I with the applicable ECLGS 5.0 coverage or provider in List-II.

List-I
 a. MSMEs
 b. Non-MSMEs
 c. Aviation
 d. Guarantee provider

List-II
 i. National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company
 ii. 90% coverage
 iii. 100% coverage
 iv. 90% coverage
options: a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are MSMEs–100% coverage, non-MSMEs–90% coverage, aviation–90% coverage, and guarantee provider–National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company. The incorrect codes interchange the coverage levels or assign the provider to a beneficiary category.

mcqs.question: Which combination correctly describes the additional-loan limit and validity of ECLGS 5.0?
options: Up to 20% of peak working capital; valid till 31 March 2027
Up to 10% of peak working capital; valid till 31 March 2026
Up to 20% of peak working capital; valid till 31 March 2026
Up to 30% of peak working capital; valid till 31 March 2027
mcqs.explanation: ECLGS 5.0 permits additional loans up to 20% of peak working capital and is valid till 31 March 2027. The other combinations change either the loan proportion or the validity date.
